append.text: **Ps 105:32 (beside *irritáre*) *quia exacerbavérunt spíritum ejus* → *porque amarguraram o seu espírito*** — D27's local decision: the root *acerbus* and the Greek παρεπίκραναν; *o seu espírito* left open between Moses' and God's. **105:43 alone → *o provocaram*.** Passed the Latinist twice.

**Ps 105:14 *concupiérunt concupiscéntiam* → *cobiçaram com cobiça*** — the proposed split applied (a craving for goods → *cobiçar*); the cognate object kept as the Portuguese figura. No reader remarked. Options *arderam de cobiça*, *ansiaram com ânsia*.

**Ps 105:24 *pro níhilo habuérunt terram* → *tiveram em nada a terra*** — with *habére* the phrase is 'count as nothing, despise' (ἐξουδένωσαν), not 55:8's adverb: v1 *tiveram por nada* was heard by the ambiguity reader as 'got it for free'; *ter em nada* is the idiom (the stylist). A local build, not a change to D44.

**Ps 105:31 *reputátum est ei in justítiam* → *lhe foi contado como justiça*** — *reputáre* is another Latin verb, so it takes its own word: *contar* (the stylist; the phrase of Gen 15:6 / Rom 4). Kept apart from *atribuir*.

**Ps 105:21 *qui fecit magnália in Ægýpto* → *que fez grandes coisas no Egito*** — copied, as the row asked; *terribília* → *coisas terríveis*. The stylist asked *grandes obras … prodígios* — refused (ópera, prodígia).
**Ps 105:35 *et factum est illis in scándalum* → *e isso se tornou para eles um tropeço*** — the row applied, 68:11's build. No remark.
**Ps 105:32 *ad aquas contradictiónis* → *junto às águas da contradição*** — the proper name keeps the cognate (MS1932); *da contenda* and *de Meribá* options. The ambiguity reader did not know it.
**Ps 105:32 *vexátus est Móyses* → *Moisés foi maltratado*** — the row applied; the Latinist (minor, v1) asked *afligido* (afflígere's) — option.

**Ps 105:33 *Et distínxit in lábiis suis* → *E pronunciou com os seus lábios.*** — the row applied; the Latinist asked *proferiu distintamente* (v1) and *distinguiu* (v2, DRB), both minor — options. A full stop before the asterisk: the ambiguity reader took the next colon as what was pronounced.
**Ps 105:46 *qui céperant eos* → *os que os tinham capturado*** — a local departure: with persons as object *tomar* is unclear; the Greek αἰχμαλωτισάντων. *tomado* option.

**Ps 105:29 *irritavérunt eum in adinventiónibus suis* → *o provocaram com as suas invenções*; 105:39 *se prostituíram nas suas invenções*** — the row applied (preposition by the verb). The ambiguity reader heard the sense of evil devices only half.
**Ps 105:39 *fornicáti sunt in adinventiónibus suis* → *se prostituíram nas suas invenções*** — decided with 72:27, as the row said.

**Ps 105:23 *si non Móyses … stetísset in confractióne* → *se Moisés … não se tivesse posto na brecha*; 105:30 *stetit Phínees* → *Finéas se pôs de pé*** — *pôr-se* for the taking of a stand, one verb in both; *confráctio* → *brecha* (L&S cite 105:23).
**Ps 105:4 *in beneplácito pópuli tui* → *no favor do vosso povo*** — the row applied (the Advent versicle); the ambiguity reader found the genitive unclear, as the Latin's.

terms: | Ps 105 names | Datan, Abiron, Horeb, Beelfegor, Finéas (MS1932's forms, 59:9's rule); Aarão, Moisés, Cam, Canaã, Egito, Mar Vermelho (as Pss 77, 104) | open | Ps 105:16–38. The ambiguity reader knew none of Datan, Abiron, Horeb, Beelfegor, Finéas — expected; the stylist asked the current *Fineias* (option). |

| initiári (+ dative, *initiáti sunt Beélphegor*) | ser iniciado em (*E foram iniciados em Beelfegor*) | open | Ps 105:28 (ἐτελέσθησαν; L&S 'initiate into mysteries'); MS1932 *consagraram-se a* option. No remark. |

| quassátio | abalo (*e cessou o abalo*) | open | Ps 105:30, only place; L&S 'a shaking; affliction', citing this verse; the Greek θραῦσις is 105:23's *confráctio* too. *flagelo* (MS1932) is flagéllum's (D39); *mortandade* (DRB) names the event. The ambiguity reader heard 'commotion'. For Gustavo. |
| saturitas | fartura (*e enviou fartura às suas almas*) | open | Ps 105:15 (πλησμονή; the Latin with the Greek against the Hebrew 'leanness'); *saciedade* (the saciar family) option. |
| laudáre laudem | louvar o louvor (*e louvaram o seu louvor*) | open | Ps 105:12 — the Latin's figura kept (the Greek ᾖσαν 'sang'); MS1932 *cantaram* option. No reader objected. |
| cito fecérunt | *Depressa o fizeram:* | open | Ps 105:13 (ἐτάχυναν); the object pronoun Portuguese needs, a colon to point it forward. The Latinist (minor, twice) asked the bare verb — held. |

| pœnitére (of God) | arrepender-se (*e se arrependeu segundo a multidão da sua misericórdia*) | open | Ps 105:45 (μετεμελήθη); DRB 'repented'; MS1932 *teve piedade* explains (option). The ambiguity reader: 'may sound like God had done wrong' — the Latin's word. Recurs 109:4 *non pœnitébit eum* (grep; 89:13 has *deprecábilis*, another verb). |

| dare in misericórdias (*dedit eos in misericórdias*) | *fez que achassem misericórdia* | open | Ps 105:46 (εἰς οἰκτιρμούς). The word-for-word *deu-os às misericórdias* was heard by the ambiguity reader as 'at the captors' mercy' — the opposite; the Latinist (v2, minor) called the fix paraphrase and asked *E os entregou às misericórdias* (option). For Gustavo. |

| clitic placement in narrative | proclisis after *E* and after a subject (*E os salvou*, *E os inimigos deles os atribularam*); enclisis only at sentence start and with imperatives | open | Ps 105 v2 (the stylist): enclitic *-nos* after a 3rd plural (*dominaram-nos*, *atribularam-nos*) is heard as 'us' in a psalm that alternates we and they; *-no* blurs into *-nos* in choir. Ps 104:37 *E os tirou* agrees. |
